$comment: Per-host SPKI pins for the MASQUE/WARP edges. Loaded by aether::trust and
validated by trust::active_pins() at startup: a host with zero unexpired
pins is a hard error, never a fallback to 'trust everyone'.
---- MEASURED 2026-09-23 (previously: digests lifted unverified from consts.rs)
Command used, from a machine with normal internet egress:
openssl s_client -connect <ip>:443 -servername <sni> -showcerts </dev/null
# and the QUIC/H3 form the tunnel actually uses:
openssl s_client -quic -alpn h3 -connect <ip>:443 -servername <sni> -showcerts
# pin over the measured leaf:
openssl x509 -in leaf.pem -pubkey -noout | openssl pkey -pubin -outform der \
| openssl dgst -sha256
FINDING 1 - the leaf is chosen by the IP dialled, NOT by the SNI presented.
The consumer-masque anycast VIPs 162.159.198.2 and 162.159.199.2 answered
every one of {consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com, consumer-masque-proxy.
cloudflareclient.com, cloudflareaccess.com} over TCP TLS 1.3 and over QUIC/
h3 (ALPN h3 negotiated) with the SAME certificate: subject CN=masque.
cloudflareclient.com, issuer C=US/O=Cloudflare, Inc./CN=2024-02-27 Self-
Signed Root, SAN DNS:masque.cloudflareclient.com only, notBefore 2026-01-26
leaf DER sha256 06e713be526c4eb81d1044df72748d4b18913cb2add84dc003ac2b97dd
123792, SPKI sha256 eb591b36ab26ba617e98371918c10bcdeae3742db6e76543f94be
524dce1d555. So both host entries below genuinely carry that one digest;
the split the previous revision left as an open guess is now measured, and
it came back as 'no split is available on this axis'.
FINDING 2 - require_hostname stays false, on evidence, not on assumption.
The live edge's SAN is DNS:masque.cloudflareclient.com. It does not contain
consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com nor consumer-masque-proxy.cloudflare-
client.com, so a name check against the dialled SNI rejects the peer the
tunnel is pointed at. (AETHER_MASQUE_SNI fronting makes the same point
sharper: the name in the ClientHello is a user-chosen third value.)
FINDING 3 - require_chain stays false, on evidence. The peer sends exactly
one certificate and its issuer is a Cloudflare-private self-signed root that
is in no trust store: OpenSSL reports 'Verify return code: 21 (unable to
verify the first certificate)' for both SNIs, TCP and QUIC. Chain building
cannot succeed here, so require_chain=true is an outage, not a tightening.
The previous revision expected the per-host split to eventually leave one
host with only chain-issued pins; FINDING 1 shows that gate cannot be met
by splitting, because both hosts are served by the same self-signed edge.
FINDING 4 - what WOULD support both checks is a different endpoint, which the
schema cannot express. The generic Cloudflare anycast edges (162.159.192.1,
188.114.97.1, engage.cloudflareclient.com) answer these same two SNIs with a
CA-issued leaf: CN=cloudflareclient.com, issuer C=US/O=Let's Encrypt/CN=YE2,
SAN DNS:*.cloudflareclient.com + DNS:cloudflareclient.com (so the name check
PASSES for both hosts), 4-certificate chain, 'Verify return code: 0 (ok)',
notBefore 2026-08-20, notAfter 2026-11-18, SPKI sha256 19cee442633f9b409e76
9d4310896f9304d67bcf81e6bcf299a674392ca041f0. That digest is deliberately
NOT added to either pin set: those edges are the control-plane/API anycast,
not a CONNECT-IP relay, and adding a pin is a widening that buys reachability
we have not asked for. Narrowing the two flags above therefore needs an
endpoint-keyed policy, not more SNI rows; that is a code change, recorded in
packaging/trust/README.md and the spec's closing inventory rather than
invented in this file.
FINDING 5 - eb591b36… is measured. The earlier 3fbb1d74… fallback
was not presented by any peer observed here - 9 IPs x
.199.2, 188.114.96.1, 188.114.97.1) and both MASQUE VIPs x both MASQUE SNIs
over QUIC/h3 - and the identity it was recorded under is contradicted: the
cloudflareaccess.com leaf issued by Google Trust Services WE1 measured on
55e716c75b2755c3f and a 90-day window (notBefore 2026-08-30, notAfter
2026-11-28), i.e. that class of leaf rotates its key quarterly and can never
be a stable MASQUE pin. The unmeasured digest was removed from both active
pin sets: retaining an unaudited key would let it authenticate a peer even
though no observed MASQUE endpoint presented it. If another region requires
that key, measure its leaf, host, expiry and SPKI there before adding it back.
SECOND-VANTAGE CHECK - run this from inside the customer network and from
at least one non-local exit against every peer the prober/session can dial:
for ip in $(< masque-vips.txt); do for sni in consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com consumer-masque-proxy.cloudflareclient.com; do
openssl s_client -connect $ip:443 -servername $sni -showcerts </dev/null 2>/dev/null \
| awk '/-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----/{n++} n' | openssl asn1parse -inform PEM \
| grep -c 3fbb1d74   # inspect any hit before considering a new pin
done; done
require_chain IS NOT OPTIONAL. The field lost its serde default because an
omitted key decoded to false, which silently discarded BoringSSL's chain
verdict on every live connection while the file appeared to declare a
policy. Every host below therefore states it.
consumer-masque-proxy.cloudflareclient.com is not consulted by any live
connection path today: quic.rs and masque_h2.rs both pass
consts::CONNECT_SNI as the pin host, and that name only appears as one of
the SNIs h3_probe.rs sweeps. Its entry is kept so that wiring it up later
fails closed against measured data instead of hitting 'no pin set for host'.
Expiry: the measured pins carry 1803513600 (2027-02-25T00:00:00Z),
one day before the observed leaf's 2027-02-26 expiry. A pin must not
appear live after the certificate it identifies is already expired.

pins.note: MEASURED 2026-09-23 at 162.159.198.2 and 162.159.199.2 over TCP TLS 1.3 and QUIC/h3 for this SNI: CN=masque.cloudflareclient.com, self-signed by Cloudflare '2024-02-27 Self-Signed Root', SAN DNS:masque.cloudflareclient.com, valid to 2027-02-26. No chain is sent and the SAN does not cover this SNI, which is the evidence behind require_chain=false and require_hostname=false above (findings 2 and 3).

MEASURED 2026-09-23: this SNI received the byte-identical leaf that consumer-masque.cloudflareclient.com received - same issuer (C=US, O=Cloudflare, Inc., CN=2024-02-27 Self-Signed Root), same SAN (DNS:masque.cloudflareclient.com, which does not name this host either), same leaf digest 06e713be…, on both VIPs, over TCP and QUIC/h3. Sharing this digest is a measurement result, not a carried-over guess: the L4 SNI does not select a different key.
